message:
test(host): time the isolated path against the one it replaced

Product 1 (comment only), test 1, build 1.

The capture was measured before the helper existed. What had not been measured is what isolation
costs on top of it -- a process creation, a mapping, a wait and a teardown, paid per preview --
and a design that trades cost for recoverability should say what the trade was.

Both numbers now come out of the same probe process in the same run, ten samples each, so the
difference is the isolation rather than two machines' worth of noise. Across three runs: the
isolated path is 66-72ms median and 106-110ms worst; the same capture called directly is 28-34ms
median and 32-47ms worst. Isolation costs roughly 37-43ms per preview, and the worst isolated
sample is about a tenth of the deadline.

So a picker with ten windows pays about two thirds of a second instead of a third, once. After
that the budget is what decides whether a window is asked again at all.

The reviewer suggested reaching the stall through a test-only argument on the helper, gated out
of the shipping build. The stall here does not need one and there is no gate to get wrong: the
host resolves its helper beside the running executable, so the test stages a scratch directory
and puts whatever it likes there under that name. Confirmed by grep -- no test-only argument
exists in either the helper or the host, and the shipped GNLinkCapture has nothing to strip.

The deadline comment now carries what the measurements do not cover, which is the part worth
reading: UWP windows cannot be created by the test, the user's running windows are out of scope,
and a window backed by a large GPU surface could cost more than anything measured. What was
tried tops out at a 1920x1080 flip-model swapchain, which cost the same as plain GDI at that
size.

16 checks, three runs clean.
